translations.answer: In the custom-gripper Unitree G1 of HuMI, and during the tasks being measured, only recording the hands is insufficient to stabilize the squat, kneel, and movement operations. Collecting hand/hip/foot trajectories and using the target robot's real-time IK preview for demonstration, combined with a high-level visuomotor interface designed for tracking error, significantly outperforms the ablations in the paper that remove preview or specify the whole-body. However, this result depends on external VIVE, skilled operators, and task-specific low-level strategies.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Robot-free demonstrations include synchronized wrist imagery and tracked hand/pelvis/foot poses.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: A target-robot IK preview is available during collection.
translations.applicability.assumptions.2: A hierarchical high-level visuomotor policy and low-level whole-body tracker execute the demonstrations.
translations.applicability.environments.1: seven training scenes and four unseen evaluation scenes for squat-and-pick
translations.applicability.simulators.0: paper-reported simulation training environment; exact public code/config unverified
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper includes real-robot task results and targeted interface ablations with large effect sizes, and the official project page corroborates the system identity and demonstrations. Confidence is capped by one robot, small 10-20 trial ablations, experienced operators, custom hardware/external tracking, and an unverified public code repository.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 2-7, Sections II-IV and VI, Appendix B-F, and Appendix Tables I-III
translations.evidence.0.note: Supports human-in-loop IK adaptation, whole-body keypoints, chunk-reference and relative-keypoint interfaces, collection throughput, task success, and deployment rates.
